title: Farik RPC
description: The JSON-RPC 2.0 text frames between the browser and the daemon's GET /rpc (docs/SPEC.md section 8). Any frame is a request, a response, or a notification; the query results and the command reply are $defs, which name the shape of each answer. command and event are objects here, not references, because one schema never references another: command_from_value and event_from_value read them.

requestId.description: The caller's own number for a request, echoed by its response.

command.description: A command wire of command.schema.json; the daemon validates it with command_from_value.

rpcRequest.title: Rpc Request
rpcRequest.description: What the browser sends. The pairing of a query's name with its params is the schema's; the meaning of a command is command_from_value's.

result.description: emptyResult for subscribe and unsubscribe, commandReply for command, the query's own result def for query, and the method's own result def (projectOpenResult, projectCreateResult, accountConnectResult, sandboxBuildResult, browserPullResult) for a setup method, and each other method's own result def.

id.description: null when the request's id could not be read.

rpcError.title: Rpc Error
rpcError.description: -32700 parse, -32600 invalid request, -32601 unknown method, -32602 invalid params, -32603 internal (the store or a file failed), -32001 unknown_query, -32002 not_found, -32003 refused_here, -32004 no_project (the daemon has no project yet, so it answers only the setup queries), -32005 refused (a setup method was refused; the message is the sentence to show).

rpcNotification.title: Rpc Notification
rpcNotification.description: The server's push of one event. The event is an object here because one schema never references another; rpc_notification_from_value reads it with event_from_value.

commandReply.title: Command Reply
commandReply.description: What the daemon's POST /command answers once the token passes (docs/SPEC.md section 8.2): what the command did, as one sentence and the sequence numbers of the events it appended, or why it did nothing. A reply is what leaves a process, so it has a schema as a command does; farik_protocol::command::reply_from_value reads it against this definition.

kind.description: invalid: the command cannot be handled as given, a schema refusal among them; refused: it cannot be done to what it names as things stand; not_found: what it names is not there; failed: the store, a file, git, or the orchestrator failed.

design_plan.description: The task's latest UI/UX Designer's plan and the Product Manager's decision on it (ADR 0026), or null when no plan was proposed. reason is the decision's, once there is one.

ui_change.description: Whether the task's change touches the interface (ADR 0026): a Software Developer's task whose contract sets ui_change, or whose branch changes a path the team's ui_paths match.

design_review.description: The UI/UX Designer's design review of the change (step 12), or null when it is not a UI change. state says where it stands; reasons and checks are the latest design_review.recorded since the task last entered verifying, when there is one.

design_reviews.description: Every design_review.recorded of the task, oldest first: the Designer that recorded it, whether it passed, its reasons, and when (step 12). The gate reads the earlier ones as the Designer's send-backs, and the latest as who signed the letter.

team.description: The team file as team.schema.json shapes it.

max_agents.description: The most agents a team may have that are not retired (spec 4.1).

sandboxed.description: Whether sessions run in Docker's sandbox. False in no-sandbox mode, where a command an agent runs can reach a connector's keys (spec 8.6), so no page promises that the agent never sees them.

connectors.description: Each agent's custom MCP servers and whether each runs (ADR 0030): connected when the definition kept on this machine beside its keys is the team file's and every key it names is kept; connect_again when none is kept or the team file changed since, or, for a kit's service, when the kit's tags or fields changed with a release (ADR 0036), so it runs nothing until the user connects it again; sign_in_again when the service ended the agent's sign-in, so it runs nothing until the user signs in again; not_in_kit when a kit's service is no longer in its agent's role's kit, so the page offers Remove alone (ADR 0036); store_unavailable when the keychain or the private file could not be read, the last time Farik read it, so it is left out of sessions until it can be. The kept definition is read once per connect and disconnect, when a session is set up, and the first time it is asked for.

auth.description: How the server is reached with the user's authority: keys the user gave, or a sign-in to the service (ADR 0033).

revokes.description: For a server signed in to: whether the service has a way to be asked to forget the sign-in when it is removed. Absent for a server with keys.

provider.description: For a server signed in to with one of Farik's own apps: what the app is called (GitHub), which the page names in place of the server's address (step 03b).

settings_url.description: For the same: the page at the service where the user removes Farik's app, which Remove's confirmation links to.

stored_in.description: Where the agent's keys for this server are kept, when an entry is: the computer's keychain, or a private file only the user can read. Absent when none is kept or the store could not be read.

source.description: Where the server came from: the user's own, or a service of the agent's role's kit (ADR 0036).

kits.description: Each role on the team whose kit has a service to connect by name, with the copy the page shows (ADR 0036). A container connector, which Farik runs itself, is not listed, and nor is a role with no service.

key_page.description: Where the key is made; present when the service takes keys.

labels.description: A tool to what it does in the user's words.

allowances.description: What the kit lets the user pre-approve (ADR 0037): each spending tool with its default calls each period and the plural noun for what a call makes. Present when the kit offers any.

project_root.description: null while the daemon is in setup mode, before a project is chosen.

take_on_error.description: Why taking the chosen project on failed, or null.

setup_pending.description: Whether the project was just set up and waits for the team's setup (the marker .farik/local/setup-pending).

design_review_state.description: tasks.list only, for a task in verifying whose change is to the interface: task.get's design_review.state, so the board need not ask each card (step 12).

backlog.description: Whether the row waits in the Backlog for a sprint (ADR 0028): farik-core's in_the_backlog, so the board need not work it out again.

taskProjection.description: One row of the board (farik_store::TaskProjection). Optional fields are absent, not null, when the projection has none.

designer_browser.description: The UI/UX Designer's browser, the Playwright connector's pinned image; present only for a team with a Designer, which setup's suggested team has (step 12).

environment_variable.description: The variable the credential comes from, when it comes from the environment: Farik cannot remove it, so the page names it rather than offering Disconnect.

key_refused.description: True while the team is paused because the model provider refused the credential (docs/SPEC.md 5.5): the key did not work, and connecting the account again resumes the team. Left out otherwise.

taking_on.description: True when a project that waited on the credential is now being taken on, so the daemon restarts on it.

browserPullRequest.title: Browser Pull Request
browserPullRequest.description: Setup pulls the UI/UX Designer's browser, the Playwright connector's image, by its pinned digest (step 12).

contract.description: A contract as task-contract.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

taskScreenshotQuery.title: Task Screenshot Query
taskScreenshotQuery.description: A screenshot farik_check_page took of the task's preview (step 12): file is the name one of the task's page.checked events gives, and any other name is not_found.

requestFileRequest.title: Request File Request
requestFileRequest.description: Files the person's words as a draft request. Answers requestFileResult; a refusal of words under 20 characters carries data with errors, each a path, a message and a code, the code too_short, as team.validate answers them.

text.description: The request in the person's words: its first line is the title, and the whole is the intent. The daemon refuses a text under 20 characters.

from_chat_message.description: The seq of the agent's chat reply whose proposed request this is: the reply must carry a request not already sent, or the daemon refuses with a sentence. task.created records it.

contract.description: A contract as task-contract.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

waitingListResult.description: What waits on the human, questions first, then connector calls waiting to be allowed (tool_approval, each with approval, the seq of its tool_approval.requested, its server, its bare tool name, and its whole input as compact JSON, which only that kind carries), then marketing plans waiting for the owner (marketing_plan, whose title is the plan's and whose line is "<agent name> proposes a marketing plan: <title>", each with plan, its id, its summary, its total budget as a decimal string, its currency, and its first and last day, which only that kind carries), then posts outside the plan waiting for the owner (social_post, whose title is its task's and whose line is "<agent name> wants to post on <Network>", each with post, its number, channel, text, media, the pictures and clips as their addresses with kind image or video, and at, when it would go out in the offset it was written in, which only that kind carries; a post that was decided or whose time came is no longer listed), approvals, other escalations, acceptances, and integrations; then the UI changes whose design review waits for the team's preview (preview_missing), for Docker's sandbox (designer_needs_sandbox), or for Playwright to be turned on for the Designer (designer_needs_browser).

contract.description: A contract as task-contract.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

contractCheckResult.description: The rules an unsaved plan fails: schema errors first, as rule schema, then the Definition of Ready's; total is the number of checks run, the schema counting as one.

taskDiffResult.description: A task's diff against the integration branch, or an epic's tasks' integrated diffs joined in id order, each under a # FRK-n line.

taskChecksResult.description: Each criterion's latest result since the task last entered verifying; for a plan awaiting approval, the Definition of Ready's failures, each named by its rule.

taskTriesResult.description: The try in progress, iteration + 1, of max_iterations + 1 plus the extra tries granted: the limit bounds returns, and the pass after the last return is a try too.

sprintCurrentResult.description: The open sprint and how many of its tasks are done (accepted or cancelled), or null when none is open.

escalationChoicesResult.description: What the human may do about an escalation: each choice's label and the command the page sends, to which it adds the message.

contractSaveResult.description: The human's edit is saved; back_to_refining says a frozen plan went back to refining, to be checked and approved again.

taskCostsResult.description: What a task has spent, by the purposes' plain words (Planning: triage, refine, plan; Building: implement; Checking: verify; Meetings and talk: ceremony, conversation; Conversations: chat), each word that has spent anything, and its contract's limit.

sprintRow.description: A sprint: its file, who started it (sprint.started), the first assigner that planned it (null when only Farik did), what it spent, and how many of its tasks are done (accepted or cancelled).

backlogSummaryResult.description: Whether the team plans its work in sprints, and how much work waits in its Backlog: the rows with no parent, so an epic counts once (ADR 0028).

sprintGetResult.description: sprintRow's fields, its tasks, and its meetings: the ceremony posts from its start until the next sprint starts, one meeting per ceremony session, oldest first.

marketingPlanListResult.description: Every marketing plan, newest first (docs/SPEC.md 6.5; ADR 0042): its id, title, state, dates, currency and total budget as a decimal string with two decimals, the agent that proposed it and the task it waited on the owner for, and when it was proposed. state is proposed (waiting for the owner), returned (sent back), approved (approved, and not the plan in force: not started, or another is active), active (approved, and the plan in force today) or ended.

marketingPlanGetResult.description: One marketing plan whole (docs/SPEC.md 6.5; ADR 0042): what was proposed, its state as in marketing_plan.list, the owner's decision with their words (note for an approval, empty when they added nothing; reason for a plan sent back) and when, or null while it waits, and its end with why and when, the owner's note when they ended it with one and the plan that replaced it when a newer plan did, or null. text is the plan's text, to be shown as text and never rendered as markup. Refused not_found for a plan nobody proposed.

written_posts.description: The posts the Marketing Specialist wrote for this plan's slots, oldest first, each with where it stands: a slot may have several, an earlier one failed, missed or stopped and a newer one written for it. at is when it goes out, in the offset it was written in; state_at is when it reached that state. stopped_by (owner, declined or plan_ended) is there for a stopped post, and missed_why for a missed one. text is shown as text and never rendered as markup.

note.description: What the owner said when they ended the plan, as they wrote it; left out when they said nothing.

replaced_by.description: The plan that took its place, when why is replaced.

socialPostsListResult.description: The posts Today shows (docs/SPEC.md 6.5; ADR 0042): every post scheduled or sent whose time is still ahead, soonest first, then every post missed or failed in the last 24 hours, the latest first. A post stopped, one still waiting for the owner (waiting.list has it), and one whose time passed unsent are not here. at is when it goes out, in the offset it was written in; hands_over_at is when Farik hands it to Buffer, in UTC: an hour before at, or later for a post the owner allowed later than that. approved_by is plan or owner; plan and slot are there for a plan's post. missed_why is there for a missed post and reason, Farik's sentence then Buffer's words, for a failed one: both are shown as text, never as markup.

socialPostMediaRequest.title: Social Post Media Request
socialPostMediaRequest.description: One picture of a post, fetched by the daemon, since the browser may not load pictures from other sites. Answers socialPostMediaResult; refused not_found for an unknown post or picture, for a clip (the page opens its address in a new tab), and for an address that is not public, is gone, is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP picture (never an SVG), or is over 20 MiB.

allowancesListResult.description: What each connected kit connector of an active agent lets it make without asking, and how many it has made this period (docs/SPEC.md 6.7, ADR 0037): the period, the open sprint's or, with none open, the UTC day's since the later of its start and the last sprint's end, and one row per allowance. used counts every call of the tool in the period, those a grant allowed among them, so it may exceed of. what is the kit's plural noun for what a call makes.

costsSummaryResult.description: Today's spending (UTC) and the team's daily limit, today's one-to-one chats (purpose chat), the last sprint's (the open one while one is), and each agent's that is not retired, in the team's order.

metricsResult.description: The harness metrics of F17, over the project or one sprint; a rate is null while no task is accepted.

teamProposeQuery.title: Team Propose Query
teamProposeQuery.description: The team setup suggests: the team as it is with the five suggested agents in place of its own, and the criterion library as it is, which the setup form edits beside it.

teamValidateQuery.title: Team Validate Query

team.description: A team as team.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

teamValidateQuery.description: A changed team checked and described before it is saved (docs/SPEC.md section 10). Nothing is written.

modelsListQuery.title: Models List Query
modelsListQuery.description: The newest model of each family the price table prices, with the words a person reads for it.

teamSaveRequest.title: Team Save Request
teamSaveRequest.description: Writes the team when it has no errors and appends team.updated. It refuses a status change (an agent is paused, retired or resumed from its card) and removing an agent the log has seen work from. Answers emptyResult; a refusal's data holds errors, each a path, a message and a code, as team.validate answers them.

team.description: A team as team.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

teamStartRequest.title: Team Start Request
teamStartRequest.description: The setup form's Start the team: writes the team and the criteria, removes the setup marker, and appends team.updated, criteria.updated and, when the marker was there and the team is paused, team.resumed: without the marker a paused team stays paused. While the marker is there it may replace the starter team's agents. Answers emptyResult.

team.description: A team as team.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

criteria.description: A criterion library as criteria.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

criteriaSaveRequest.title: Criteria Save Request
criteriaSaveRequest.description: Writes the criterion library when it is one and appends criteria.updated. Answers emptyResult.

criteria.description: A criterion library as criteria.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

accountDisconnectRequest.title: Account Disconnect Request
accountDisconnectRequest.description: Deletes the AI account's credential from every store that holds it and, when one did, pauses the team. A credential from the environment cannot be removed: nothing is deleted, and the answer names its variable.

team.description: A team as team.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

criteria.description: A criterion library as criteria.schema.json shapes it; the daemon validates it.

unavailable.description: The proposed agents this computer cannot run, which setup shows unticked: the UI/UX Designer, with designer_needs_sandbox, where Farik runs without Docker's sandbox (step 12, D3).

effects.description: Each effect of the change in plain words; empty when there are errors.

agents.description: The team as it would be, as team.get answers it; left out when there are errors.

judges.description: Left out when there are errors.

paused.description: Whether this call paused the team: true only when a credential was removed and the team was running. A team already paused stays paused and answers false.

environment_variable.description: The variable the credential comes from, when it comes from the environment and so could not be removed.

projectScanQuery.title: Project Scan Query
projectScanQuery.description: The project scanned again, as the setup screen "What we found" reads it back in rows. Nothing is written.

projectNoteRequest.title: Project Note Request
projectNoteRequest.description: Something is wrong: the user's words kept in .farik/project.md under "The user says", which every rescan carries across. Answers emptyResult.

text.description: What the user says about the project, in their own words.

language.description: The language with the most tracked files.

workspace.description: Whether the project is a workspace.

packages.description: How many packages the workspace has.

tests_in.description: Where the tests are, as a location.

last_commit.description: How long ago the last commit was, in words; null before the first commit.

checks.description: The text of each check the scan found in the project's own commands.

kept_private.description: The protected-path globs that match something on disk, walked four folders deep without .git and node_modules, over at most 2000 entries.

connectorServer.description: A service as the user connects it, before its tools are labelled: either a custom MCP server, an mcp_servers entry of team.schema.json without tools (name, transport, and command and args, or url and headers, credential_keys, and oauth for a web address the user signs in to; source, when given, is custom), held to validate_team as the agent's entry; or a service of the agent's role's kit, { name, source: kit }, a form of its own that carries nothing else, so a browser cannot send fields the kit decides (ADR 0036).

kitServer.description: A service of the agent's role's kit, by name: the daemon builds its entry from the kit (kit_entry), its tags included. connector.connect with it takes tags {} (kit_names_these otherwise); a name the agent's role's kit does not have is connector_not_in_kit.

connectorKeys.description: Each of the server's keys by name, with its value. Never echoed: a refusal of these params carries no data.

connectorToolsRequest.title: Connector Tools Request
connectorToolsRequest.description: Lists a custom MCP server's tools, started or reached with the agent's keys, or with the sign-in an attempt made when the server has oauth, as ConnectorAdd's second step shows them (docs/SPEC.md 5.6; ADRs 0030 and 0033). Nothing is kept, and the attempt is not used up. A server with oauth and no attempt is refused sign_in_needed; an attempt that is unknown, used, expired, unfinished, or another server's is refused sign_in_unknown. A refusal of these params carries no data, as account.connect's does.

usable.description: False for a name Claude Code would rewrite (outside ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$): Farik can't use this tool, and it is never written to the team file.

connectorConnectRequest.title: Connector Connect Request
connectorConnectRequest.description: Gives the agent a custom MCP server (docs/SPEC.md 5.6, 6.7; ADR 0030): its tools listed with the keys, each usable one labelled by tags or else external_effect, the keys kept in the keychain or a private file beside the definition's spec_sha256, then connector_connect handled, which writes the team file and appends connector.connected. A server with oauth takes attempt, a finished sign-in, in place of keys, and uses it up; its grant is kept where keys are, and a grant it replaces is asked to be forgotten. A refusal of these params carries no data, as account.connect's does; a refusal of the entry carries the team's errors, each at its field.

tags.description: The user's label for each tool by name; a listed tool not named here is external_effect.

connectorAllowances.description: How many calls each period the agent makes of each spending tool without asking (ADR 0037), 0 to 1000; the daemon refuses one outside it allowance_out_of_range, and one for a tool the kit gives none allowance_not_offered. A kit service only; left out at a connect, each tool starts at the kit's default.

connectorAllowancesRequest.title: Connector Allowances Request
connectorAllowancesRequest.description: Changes a kit connector's allowances without its key typed again (docs/SPEC.md 6.7; ADR 0037): the kept entry must be the team file's (connector_not_confirmed), the numbers are checked as connect checks them over the ones the entry holds, the same keys or sign-in are kept beside the new entry's hash, then connector_connect is handled, which writes the team file and appends connector.connected. A kit that has changed the service is connector_not_in_kit: connect it again. A tool left out keeps its number. Answers emptyResult.

stored_in.description: Where the keys were kept: the computer's keychain, or a private file only the user can read.

tools.description: Each tool as it was written to the team file, with its label.

signInAttempt.description: A sign-in under way, held in the daemon's memory for ten minutes, bound to the agent and the server (name, url and oauth) it was made for, and used up by connector.connect.

connectorSignInRequest.title: Connector Sign In Request
connectorSignInRequest.description: Starts signing the agent in to the service of a web-address server (docs/SPEC.md 6.7; ADR 0033): finds how the server offers it, registers Farik as a client or uses the one the server names, opens a listener for the way back on this computer's loopback, and answers the address the user opens in the browser. A new attempt for the same agent and server ends the old one. Refused sign_in_not_offered (the server does not say it can be signed in to), sign_in_not_supported (it does, and Farik has no way to register), pkce_not_supported, or sign_in_failed, each as the message's first word and a colon. server is the object connector.tools takes, and holds oauth.

authorize_url.description: The service's page, which the browser opens. No token is in it.

issuer.description: Who signs the user in, as the service says. Its host is what the page names; it can differ from the server's, as Stripe's sign-in is at access.stripe.com.

provider.description: What Farik's own app for the service is called (GitHub), when one signs the user in: the page names it in place of the issuer's host (step 03b).

user_code.description: The short code the user types on authorize_url, for an app that signs in with a code (the device flow). The code Farik polls with is never sent.

install_url.description: Where the user installs Farik's own app on what the agent is to read, when it must be (a private repository on GitHub).

connectorSignInStatusRequest.title: Connector Sign In Status Request
connectorSignInStatusRequest.description: How an attempt is going. Refused sign_in_unknown for one that is not known, was used up, ended, or expired. Never answers a token.

connectorSignInCancelRequest.title: Connector Sign In Cancel Request
connectorSignInCancelRequest.description: Ends an attempt because the person pressed Cancel (docs/SPEC.md 6.7): its polling or its listener stops, and whatever the service says afterwards, or said already, is dropped, so a sign-in approved after Cancel is never kept. Answers emptyResult, also for an attempt that is already gone or was used up, since there is nothing left to end.

message.description: Farik's words for the step that failed and, where there was one, the HTTP status. It quotes nothing the service sent.

connectorTag.description: A connector tool's label (docs/SPEC.md 5.6): network, only reads; external_effect, changes something outside the sandbox; denied, never offered.

connectorDisconnectRequest.title: Connector Disconnect Request
connectorDisconnectRequest.description: Takes a custom MCP server away from the agent: connector_disconnect handled, which removes its team file entry and appends connector.disconnected, then its keys deleted from wherever they are kept; another agent's are never touched. Answers emptyResult.

agentReplaceRequest.title: Agent Replace Request
agentReplaceRequest.description: Replace: the agent retired and a newcomer added, in one validated change to the team file, so that a team is never left without the role the agent held. Appends agent.updated, then team.updated. Answers emptyResult; a refusal's data holds errors, each a path, a message and a code, as team.validate answers them, as team.save's does.

newcomer.description: The agent that joins, as team.schema.json shapes an agent; the daemon validates the team it makes.

effectiveAgent.title: Effective Agent
effectiveAgent.description: An agent as its sessions run: its model and effort (its own, or else its role's), the model's words, the tiers it holds, and base_tiers, those its role and the team's permission answers give it before its own grants and revokes.

label.description: The family's words, with (older) when a newer one of the family is priced; the id when no family names it.

planJudges.title: Plan Judges
planJudges.description: Who checks plans under each choice of policy.judgment.judge: the first active agent of the role, and under auto the one Team::judge resolves (spec 5.3); null where no active agent holds it.

settingsDefaultsQuery.title: Settings Defaults Query
settingsDefaultsQuery.description: What putting a setting back puts back (spec 10): farik_core::team::defaults(), the same values farik init writes.

budgets.description: The team's budgets as team.schema.json shapes them, with no daily limit.

policy.description: The starter policy, with the plan check and the permission answers written out.

rules.description: The rules the team adds to Farik's; none by default.

ui_paths.description: The UI paths every team starts with (spec 5.12): a Software Developer's change that touches one is design-reviewed.

channelMessagesQuery.title: Channel Messages Query
channelMessagesQuery.description: The team channel's newest page of messages before before_seq, or the newest of all without it (spec 5.9).

chatsListQuery.title: Chats List Query
chatsListQuery.description: The chat list (spec 4.3, 5.9): Team's newest line, then each agent's one-to-one chat.

chatLine.title: Chat Line
chatLine.description: A chat's or the channel's newest message.

chatsListResult.description: team_last is the channel's newest message.posted that is not Farik's system line; chats holds every agent of the team in the team's order, retired ones too with retired true, each with its chat's newest chat_message.posted.

chatMessagesQuery.title: Chat Messages Query
chatMessagesQuery.description: One agent's one-to-one chat, its newest page of messages before before_seq, or the newest of all without it (spec 4.3).

chatMessagesResult.description: One page of the agent's chat_message.posted, oldest first within the page: seq and at from the envelope, and the body's author, text (line breaks kept), in_reply_to and request, null when it has none; sent_as is the request the user sent a reply's proposal as (request.file's from_chat_message), null when not sent. waiting says why the user's newest message has no answer yet, null when the agent answered or nobody wrote; when several reasons apply the first wins: retired, key_refused (the team is paused because the provider refused the key), day_spent (the team's daily budget; the message is kept), asleep with until, answering (a session answers or is about to), no_answer (a session ended without a reply: the user asks again). No event is written for a chat that did not run (ADR 0026).

channelMessagesResult.description: One page of message.posted, oldest first within the page: seq and at from the envelope, task_id the task the message is about, and the body's fields, thread and in_reply_to null when it has none.

teamError.title: Team Error
teamError.description: One reason a team is refused: where, the daemon's sentence for a log, and the code the page words it by.

code.description: The refusal as the page words it for a person; the message is for a log, and invalid is any refusal with no words of its own.

templatesListQuery.title: Templates List Query
templatesListQuery.description: The saved teams on this computer, each whole, and the files in the templates folder that are not one. Every template query and method is refused with -32005 and the code no_state_folder at / when Farik has no state folder.

skillsListQuery.title: Skills List Query
skillsListQuery.description: The skills one agent has (docs/SPEC.md 6.7; ADR 0034): its role's, the team's and its own, each with how it stands for that agent. An agent the team does not have is -32002.

skillGetQuery.title: Skill Get Query
skillGetQuery.description: Every file of the team's or one agent's skill name, as its folder holds them now, for the person to read (docs/SPEC.md 6.7; ADR 0034). A folder that is not there is -32002; one the checks refuse, a file that is not UTF-8 text among them (skill_file_not_text), is refused with -32005 and a message starting with the refusal's skill_* code, and no files. An agent level names its agent, a team level names none and a role level names its role; any other is refused with -32005. A role level answers the SKILL.md Farik ships for that role, with no hash.

role.description: A role level's role id, such as software_developer.

description.description: When the skill applies, as its SKILL.md says; empty when that cannot be read.

state.description: in_use: it loads in the agent's sessions (a role's, unless replaced). replaced: another level's skill of the same name stands in its place. review: its folder, its pin and this computer's confirmation do not agree, or a check refuses it; it waits for the person to read and confirm it. missing: pinned, and its folder is not there.

bytes.description: The folder's total size; 0 when missing; a role's, its SKILL.md's.

skillsListResult.description: skills.list's answer: the agent's skills, role rows first, then the team's, then its own, each in the order its list holds. Role rows are read-only.

skillGetResult.description: skill.get's answer: files maps each path to its text as the folder holds it, sha256 is skill_sha256 of the folder (the hash skill_confirm is given; a role level answers none, since a shipped skill is trusted and pinned in the binary), and ignored_fields names the frontmatter keys other than name and description, which Farik drops from a session's copy.

templatePreviewQuery.title: Template Preview Query

slug.description: The saved team's file name without .yaml, as templates.list answers it.

templatePreviewQuery.description: What using a saved team would make of this project's team: who stays, joins, is retired or removed, the effects in words, and the errors that would refuse it. Nothing is written. A slug with no file is -32002; a file that is not a template is refused with template_unreadable at /slug.

templateSaveRequest.title: Template Save Request
templateSaveRequest.description: Saves this project's team as a template under name, in the state folder, and records no event. A name whose slug another template holds is refused with template_exists at /name unless replace is true; a name with no letter or digit, with template_name at /name. Answers templateSlugResult.

name.description: The saved team's name, as the person typed it; the daemon trims it.

replace.description: Write over the template that holds the name's slug.

templateApplyRequest.title: Template Apply Request
templateApplyRequest.description: Uses a saved team on this project: worked out again from the team as it is now, so a preview gone stale applies nothing wrong, then the team written once, each retirement's effects (agent.updated, and each in_progress task it held blocked), and team.updated with the template's name. Answers templateAppliedResult, its errors empty; a result the team's rules refuse is refused with -32005, writing nothing, and data.errors as template.preview answers them; so is a template whose file changed since its preview, with template_changed at /digest.

slug.description: The saved team's file name without .yaml, as templates.list answers it.

digest.description: The digest template.preview answered with what it showed. A template file whose bytes differ since then (saved again, or edited by hand) is refused with template_changed at /digest, writing nothing, so its answers are applied only as the preview showed them.

templateRenameRequest.title: Template Rename Request
templateRenameRequest.description: Gives a saved team another name, keeping when it was saved, and records no event. A new slug another template holds is refused with template_exists at /name. Answers templateSlugResult.

slug.description: The saved team's file name without .yaml, as templates.list answers it.

name.description: The saved team's name, as the person typed it; the daemon trims it.

templateDeleteRequest.title: Template Delete Request
templateDeleteRequest.description: Removes a saved team's file, readable or not, and records no event. Answers emptyResult.

slug.description: The saved team's file name without .yaml, as templates.list answers it.

folder.description: The folder the daemon keeps saved teams in, as it uses it: under XDG_CONFIG_HOME when that is set.

template.description: The template whole, as team-template.schema.json shapes it.

unreadable.description: The files that are not a template, by slug.

templateAppliedResult.description: template.preview's answer, and template.apply's as applied.

digest.description: The sha256 of the template file's bytes as this answer read them, in lowercase hex; template.apply is given it.

team.description: The team as it would be, or is, as team.schema.json shapes it.

retired.description: Agents that have worked and are retired, by id.

removed.description: Agents that never worked and leave the file, by id.

added.description: Agents that join, by the id each gets.

effects.description: Each effect on the agents that stay and on the team's answers, in plain words.

errors.description: Why the result is not a team; empty when it is.

slug.description: The file name the template is kept under.
